title: Fit a production replica inside the fleet envelope
description: Change topology, scheduler, context, and concurrency, then remove a GPU. The model exposes why sharding can improve memory fit while reducing independent failure domains.
notice: This is a planning model, not a hardware benchmark. Validate weight, workspace, cache, collective, and latency assumptions on the exact release bundle.

topologies.label: Independent replicas
topologies.detail: A complete model runs on each GPU. The fleet has the most independent serving groups when weights and live state fit.

topologies.label: Two-way tensor parallel
topologies.detail: Each layer is split across two GPUs. Per-device memory falls, but collectives enter every token step.

topologies.label: Two-stage pipeline
topologies.detail: Layer ranges are split across two stages. Per-device memory falls, while stage balance and bubbles matter.

topologies.label: Tensor plus pipeline
topologies.detail: Four GPUs form one serving group. The largest memory partition also creates the fewest independent groups.

schedulers.label: Static request batches
schedulers.detail: A batch holds its slots until the grouped execution completes, so early-finishing sequences can strand capacity.

schedulers.label: Continuous batching
schedulers.detail: Completed sequences release slots and compatible queued work can join at the next iteration boundary.
